paragraphs: R’ Yehoshua ben Elisha. (A Tanna of a baraita).

In [Nazir 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.44a.2-3), a baraita relates that the father of Rabbi Yitzchak, a priest according to [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Nazir.44a.2.2), died in Ginzak. Rabbi Yitzchak asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Elisha and the four elders with him. They interpreted “for his father” to mean when his father’s body was whole. Hyman compares [Moed Katan 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.20a.16) and [Tractate Semachot 12](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Semachot.12.2), taking them as mistaken versions of the story. He discusses the matter at length under Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok.[^1]

notes.text: [Hyman, vol. II, p. 621](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=204) reads בטעות הסיפור הזה (“a mistake in this story”); the supplied Hebrew has בשעת הסיפור הזה. The discussion under Rabbi Elazar begins on [Hyman, vol. I, p. 201](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._I._1910.pdf#page=232). Moed Katan names Rabbi Tzadok and Elisha ben Avuyah. Semachot names Rabbi Tzadok and describes his mourning without naming anyone he consulted. Compare [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1772&lang=en).
